newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan rupee ends firm on high money mkt rates.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan rupee ends firm on high money mkt rates.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee closed steady against the dollar on Thursday on high money market rates despite considerable dollar buying aimed at covering imports, dealers said.
The rupee ended at its opening level of 55.79, which was a shade firmer from Wednesday's close of 55.80.
"Import covering pressure was neutralised by high money rates," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
The rupee hit a low of 55.85 as a state bank continued covering for a petroleum bill, but regained its strength when high money rates forced banks to sell dollars, dealers said.

The overnight call money rate closed at 16 percent after rising to 25 percent, when five big borrowers including two state banks, entered the market, dealers said. The rate closed at 16 percent on Wednesday.
"Money eased near the close when one big state borrower left the market," said the Standard Chartered dealer.
The Central Bank kept its dollar-rupee exchange rate unchaged in line with the U.S. unit's steady movements overseas. Buying and selling were at 55.4648 and 56.5853.
